title: Supply-chain attestation
description: Measured truth about the running binary, plus the declared release-verification contract — what ships with every release and exactly how to verify it. Nothing is re-verified in the browser.
forbidden: Viewing the attestation contract requires the compliance:read permission.

disclaimer.body: The project is beta: no releases exist yet and the release pipeline is written but not activated. The running-binary panel is MEASURED from this process; the contract tabs are the declared contract, not a published release or a live cryptographic verification — this console never re-verifies signatures in the browser.
disclaimer.declaredRef: Declared reference — AsOf {{date}}. Sourced verbatim from docs/RELEASE-VERIFICATION.md, SECURITY.md, .goreleaser.yaml and the release / scorecard / patch-velocity workflows. The engine cannot observe repository or CI state, so this half is not served live.

live.title: Running binary (measured)
live.description: What THIS engine process can prove about itself — read live from the binary (ldflags, debug.ReadBuildInfo, crypto/fips140, a self-hash of the executable) — and the honest release state: nothing is published or verified until a v* tag fires the pipeline.
live.vcsAvailable: VCS settings stamped by the Go toolchain
live.selfHashHint: The self-SHA256 is a stream hash of the running executable, computed once at first read. Compare it OFFLINE against a future signed checksums.txt — the browser never verifies signatures, and a hash alone proves identity, not provenance.

artifacts.title: Release artifacts
artifacts.description: What ships with a release and how each artifact's trust is established. Keyless (Fulcio/Rekor) and key-based (air-gap) signing are both first-class — neither is canonical.
artifacts.identityNote: Keyless signing identity (declared): OIDC issuer {{issuer}} · cosign certificate identity {{regexp}}

slsa.title: SLSA build provenance
slsa.description: In-toto / ITE-6 provenance generated by slsa-github-generator and verified with slsa-verifier.
slsa.honesty: L3 by construction: signing runs in an isolated context the build steps cannot reach. The reusable workflow is pinned by semver tag (not SHA) — slsa-verifier validates the builder ID against the tag, so a SHA pin would break verification. Not every dependency is SHA-pinned.

sbom.title: Software bill of materials (SBOM)
sbom.description: SPDX 2.3 and CycloneDX 1.6 per archive and for the container image, attached as a signed in-toto attestation.

cisa.title: CISA minimum-elements checklist
cisa.draft: The CISA 2025 SBOM "minimum elements" are a draft (pre-decisional, public-comment) — NOT law or a finalized federal requirement. The linter fails when a field type is wholly absent (hard) and warns on the per-component omissions the draft itself permits (soft).

vex.title: OpenVEX statements
vex.description: Reachability-driven exploitability statements (govulncheck), attached as a signed in-toto attestation.

scorecard.title: OpenSSF Scorecard
scorecard.description: The four supply-chain checks that matter most for a self-hosted security product.

gauge.title: Scorecard checks declared
gauge.summary: {{declared}} of {{total}} tracked OpenSSF Scorecard checks are declared in the contract. This is a coverage count of declared checks, not a numeric Scorecard score.
gauge.caption: declared

sla.title: CVE remediation SLA
sla.description: Remediation targets from the moment a fix is available upstream for a vulnerability reachable in our shipped artifacts. These take effect at the first tagged release.

airgap.title: Air-gap bundle & OCI Helm chart
airgap.description: An offline-verifiable bundle and a dual-signed OCI Helm chart. Nothing in this path calls out.
airgap.bundleIntro: The key-based path needs no Rekor or Fulcio. Maintainers build a self-contained bundle online once; the disconnected site verifies and mirrors it.
